operation: select current-kernel research thesis and publication direction for cross-border e-commerce
objective: identify the most explanatory and falsifiable finance-story thesis linking 2026 cross-border e-commerce rule changes to differentiated A-share company economics without turning the Deep article into an industry encyclopedia

evidence.summary: MOFCOM citing Customs: 2026H1 China cross-border e-commerce imports+exports about RMB1.45tn, +5.8%; exports about RMB1.16tn, +6.3%, rejecting a sector-collapse frame.
US continues suspension of duty-free de minimis treatment for covered shipments across countries, moving duty/customs costs into low-value parcel economics.
EU abolished the under-EUR150 customs-duty exemption from 1 July 2026 with a temporary EUR3 duty per item and mandatory product identifiers from 1 November 2026.
EU customs reform shifts importer responsibility toward non-EU e-commerce platforms and introduces an EU-wide small-parcel handling fee by 1 November 2026.
Huakai Yibai 2026H1 shows revenue decline alongside profit recovery and sharp divergence between pan-SKU and boutique operations.

Focus Technology 2026H1 disclosure explicitly connects small-parcel policy adjustment with helping former B2C sellers build B2B bulk-order and long-term-customer capability; MIC paid members and B2B revenue grew.
Anker Innovations 2026H1 revenue/profit/gross margin rose, but part of cost improvement came from IEEPA tariff refunds, requiring a confounder-aware brand/product interpretation.
Loctek overseas-warehouse demand did not translate mechanically into company-wide profit: H1 warehouse revenue fell slightly while FX losses materially dragged net profit.
Saiwei 2026H1 Amazon sales grew strongly while Temu fell sharply and B2B grew, disproving a blanket marketplace-collapse or Temu-generalization thesis.

CRS analysis describes PRC-linked platforms adapting after de minimis changes through local warehouses/vendors and other operating shifts, supporting an adaptation/repricing frame rather than extinction.

Prior delivered article was rejected for weak thesis, event-company linkage, full-industry dumping, originality assurance and related quality concerns; used as negative evidence only, not rule authority.

learned_items: industry aggregate growth can coexist with a deterioration in low-value parcel unit economics
the central publication question is cost absorption/pass-through capability, not generic sector growth
research completeness must be separated from publication scope
company analysis requires causal transmission and reversal conditions rather than lists
assumptions_challenged: cross-border e-commerce rule tightening implies sector-wide contraction
brand export is the only viable adaptation path
Temu weakness can be generalized to Amazon or all marketplace channels
a Deep finance article should publish the complete researched value chain

alternatives.mechanism: publish a comprehensive cross-border e-commerce value-chain map and enumerate listed-company exposures
fit_conditions: user explicitly asks for a sector handbook or value-chain reference
misfit_conditions: event-led finance article requiring a sharp thesis and retention

alternatives.mechanism: frame de minimis and tariff changes mainly as a structural beneficiary story for overseas warehouses and localized fulfillment
failure_modes: macro demand is mistaken for company profit
utilization, tail-mile, FX and capex can dominate economics
fit_conditions: company data shows broad and sustained warehouse revenue/margin conversion
misfit_conditions: Loctek evidence shows demand migration without automatic profit conversion

alternatives.mechanism: frame rule tightening as a decisive shift from low-price cross-border retail toward branded high-margin exporters
advantages: Anker provides a strong company case
fit_conditions: evidence shows brand premium is the dominant industry-wide adjustment path
misfit_conditions: company evidence shows multiple viable adaptation routes

alternatives.mechanism: frame 2026 as the retreat of low-value parcel institutional privilege, with profitability re-ranked by each business model's ability to absorb or pass through customs, compliance and fulfillment costs
advantages: reconciles aggregate growth with regulatory tightening
naturally incorporates counterexamples and reversal conditions
failure_modes: can overclaim causality if company results are attributed wholly to policy changes
requires disciplined separation of company-specific confounders
fit_conditions: aggregate volume grows while policy costs rise and company/channel outcomes diverge
misfit_conditions: evidence shows broad sector contraction or one universally dominant beneficiary path

counterexamples: Anker's growth means tighter low-value parcel rules do not imply broad exporter deterioration.
Saiwei's Amazon growth alongside Temu decline shows channel divergence rather than marketplace-wide collapse.
Loctek's warehouse revenue/profit pattern shows overseas-warehouse demand is not an automatic listed-company profit winner.
rejected_paths: use the entire researched value chain as the Deep article outline
treat overseas warehouses as a one-way beneficiary theme
reduce the story to brand-vs-low-price e-commerce
write a policy chronology followed by an unrelated listed-company list
selection_rationale: It best explains the observed combination of continued sector growth, removal of low-value parcel privileges, and sharply differentiated company/channel financial outcomes. It yields a falsifiable event-to-company finance story while preserving broad research and selective publication.

sweeps.query_or_scope: official China scale plus US/EU 2026 low-value parcel rules and first company sample
cross-company/channel counterexample sweep across seller, B2B platform, brand and warehouse cases
September-October 2026 official EU/US policy update sweep
latest September-October investor-relations and filing refresh for selected A-share cases
independent policy-research challenge to adaptation and localization thesis

saturation.stop_reason: Two consecutive materially distinct sweeps produced no decision-changing candidate, failure mode, counterexample or thesis change after official-policy and company-level evidence had converged.
unresolved_search_gaps: Final EU small-parcel handling-fee amount was not safely established from reviewed official materials and must not be invented.

verification_plan: verify core policy and industry-scale claims against first-party government/regulator sources before publication
for every core company section require trigger/change -> mechanism -> company exposure -> operating/financial expression -> verification/reversal condition
treat tariff refunds, FX, inventory changes and capital intensity as confounders rather than attributing all financial change to the regulatory event
keep the research universe broad but account for publication scope with CORE/SUPPORT/OMIT_WITH_REASON decisions
run source-compared originality checks and PublicationFitness before DELIVERY
remaining_unknowns: exact final EU small-parcel handling-fee amount
how much of each company's 2026H1 change is causal policy impact versus company-specific execution
whether post-July/November EU changes materially alter 2026H2 company mix before year-end filings
